title: Four-skill Soccer Factor Model (season level)

paper.title: Unveiling True Talent: The Soccer Factor Model for Skill Evaluation

shoot.blurb: How many shots he takes (non-penalty shots per 90 minutes).

fox.blurb: How good his chances are (expected goals per shot): finding the right spot.

sniper.blurb: Scoring more than his chances say he should (goals per expected goal).

create.blurb: Setting up team-mates' shots (key passes per 90 minutes).

intervals: 83% central posterior intervals, as in the paper

stars.default: pool quintiles of the posterior mean (1 = bottom 20%, 5 = top 20%)
stars.sniper: 3 unless the 83% interval excludes 0 (4 above, 2 below); 5 or 1 only if it also excludes +/-0.05 (a 5% edge in goals per expected goal), because finishing skill barely varies and percentiles would exaggerate tiny gaps

replacement_pool.rule: players between the 40th and 60th percentile of level-field goals/90

departures_from_paper: Season-level outcomes rather than per-match goals: the Kaggle Understat dump has no per-match lineups.
Four correlated skills (shooting, chance quality, finishing, creating) instead of a single goals alpha; the first three multiply into expected non-penalty goals per 90, on which SAR/PAR are computed.
Team strength is the team's season points per game minus the league average (paper: pre-match points gap); no home factor at season level.
One population HSGP career curve per skill over seasons observed in the window (paper: per-player within- and cross-season HSGPs).
